sentences.zh: 傅玄

translations.literal: Fu Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan.

sentences.zh: 傅玄，字休奕，北地泥陽人也。

translations.literal: Fu Xuan, courtesy name Xiuyi, was a native of Niyang in Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan, whose courtesy name was Xiuyi, came from Niyang in Beidi commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖燮，漢漢陽太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xie was Governor of Hanyang under the Han.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xie had served as Governor of Hanyang in Han times.

sentences.zh: 父幹，魏扶風太守。

translations.literal: His father Gan was Governor of Fufeng under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Fu Gan, was Governor of Fufeng under Wei.

sentences.zh: 玄少孤貧，博學善屬文，解鐘律。

translations.literal: Fu Xuan was orphaned young and poor; he was broadly learned, skilled at composing texts, and understood bells and musical temperament.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned while still young and living in want, Fu Xuan nevertheless mastered a wide range of learning, wrote well, and understood bells and pitch pipes.

sentences.zh: 性剛勁亮直，不能容人之短。

translations.literal: By nature he was stern, candid, and bluntly honest; he could not tolerate others' shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature rigid, outspoken, and blunt—unable to indulge other people's faults.

sentences.zh: 郡上計吏再舉孝廉，太尉辟，皆不就。

translations.literal: The commandery presenting officer twice nominated him for Filial and Incorrupt; the Grand Commandant summoned him—each time he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery clerk who submitted the annual accounts nominated him twice as Filial and Incorrupt, and the Grand Commandant summoned him to serve; he declined every offer.

sentences.zh: 州舉秀才，除郎中，與東海繆施俱以時譽選入著作，撰集《魏書》。

translations.literal: The province nominated him as Flourishing Talent; he was appointed Gentleman of the Palace; together with Miao Shi of Donghai he was selected on timely reputation to enter the Editorial Service and compile the Book of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The province put him forward as a Flourishing Talent, and he was made a Gentleman of the Palace. Together with Miao Shi of Donghai he was picked—on the strength of contemporary repute—for the Editorial Service to compile the Book of Wei.

sentences.zh: 後參安東、衛軍軍事，轉溫令，再遷弘農太守，領典農校尉。

translations.literal: Later he served as adjutant on the armies of Anton and of the Guards; he was transferred to be magistrate of Wen, promoted twice to Governor of Hongnong, and concurrently held the office of Colonel Director of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as staff officer on the Anton and Guards armies, then became magistrate of Wen, rose twice more to Governor of Hongnong, and held the concurrent post of Colonel Director of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 所居稱職，數上書陳便宜，多所匡正。

translations.literal: In every post he was deemed competent; he repeatedly submitted memorials on expedient measures, and much was corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he earned a reputation for competence; he sent up memorial after memorial on practical reforms, and many of his points were adopted.

sentences.zh: 五等建，封鶉觚男。

translations.literal: When the five ranks were established, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Chungu.
translations.idiomatic: When the five noble ranks were instituted, he received the barony of Chungu.

sentences.zh: 武帝為晉王，以玄為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu was Prince of Jin, he appointed Fu Xuan as Regular Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Wu was still Prince of Jin, he named Fu Xuan Regular Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，進爵為子，加附馬都尉。

translations.literal: When the abdication took place, his rank was advanced to viscount and he was additionally granted Chief Commandant of Attendant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After the abdication his title was raised to viscount, and he was also given the concurrent appointment of Chief Commandant of Attendant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 帝初即位，廣納直言，開不諱之路，玄及散騎常侍皇甫陶共掌諫職。

translations.literal: When the emperor first took the throne, he broadly welcomed straight counsel and opened a path where nothing was taboo; Fu Xuan and Regular Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary Huangfu Tao together held remonstrance duties.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the emperor ascended the throne, he encouraged blunt advice and cleared a path where nothing need be unsaid; Fu Xuan and Regular Cavalry Attendant Huangfu Tao jointly supervised remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 玄上疏曰：「臣聞先王之臨天下也，明其大教，長其義節。

translations.literal: Fu Xuan submitted a memorial: "Your servant has heard that when former kings faced All under Heaven, they clarified the great teachings and nurtured moral principle.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan presented a memorial: "I have heard that when the sage-kings faced the realm, they made clear the great teachings and cultivated moral duty.

sentences.zh: 道化隆于上，清議行於下，上下相奉，人懷義心。

translations.literal: The Way's transforming influence flourished above and pure discussion ran below; high and low upheld one another, and every person cherished a sense of right.
translations.idiomatic: The transforming influence of the Way flourished at court, while honest opinion held sway in the countryside; ruler and ruled reinforced each other, and every heart held fast to what was right.

sentences.zh: 亡秦蕩滅先王之制，以法術相禦，而義心亡矣。

translations.literal: The lost Qin swept away the former kings' institutions, governed one another with legal methods and techniques, and the sense of right perished.
translations.idiomatic: The lost house of Qin tore down the institutions of the ancient kings, ruled by legal technique alone, and the moral sense of the people collapsed.

sentences.zh: 近者魏武好法術，而天下貴刑名；

translations.literal: In recent times Emperor Wu of Wei favored legal methods, and All under Heaven esteemed penal names;
translations.idiomatic: In Wei times Emperor Wu doted on legalist methods, and the empire learned to prize harsh statutory doctrine;

sentences.zh: 魏文慕通達，而天下賤守節。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei admired easy breadth, and All under Heaven despised holding to integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen admired fashionable cleverness and loose liberality, and the empire came to scorn steadfast integrity.

sentences.zh: 其後綱維不攝，而虛無放誕之論盈於朝野，使天下無復清議，而亡秦之病復發於今。

translations.literal: Thereafter the net of norms was not drawn tight, and idle, reckless doctrines of emptiness filled court and countryside, so that All under Heaven no longer had pure discussion, and the sickness of the lost Qin has broken out again in our day.
translations.idiomatic: After that the bonds of moral order slackened; idle talk of voidness and reckless license flooded court and capital until honest public judgment vanished—the malady of Qin has returned in our own age.

sentences.zh: 陛下聖德，龍興受禪，弘堯、舜之化，開正直之路，體夏禹之至儉，綜殷周之典文，臣詠歎而已，將又奚言！

translations.literal: "Your Majesty's sagely virtue, rising as a dragon to receive the abdication, spreads the transformation of Yao and Shun, opens the road of uprightness, embodies the utmost frugality of Yu of Xia, and weaves together the canonical texts of Yin and Zhou—your servant can only chant praise; what more is there to say!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's virtue, like a dragon's rise at the acceptance of the mandate, carries forward the reforming example of Yao and Shun, opens the way of honest counsel, embraces the deep austerity of Yu, and gathers the classical heritage of Yin and Zhou—I can only stand back in admiration; what is left for me to say?

sentences.zh: 惟未舉清遠有禮之臣，以敦風節；

translations.literal: Only you have not yet promoted ministers who are pure, remote, and courteous, to thicken moral bearing;
translations.idiomatic: Only this remains: you have not yet elevated officials who are principled, aloof, and ceremonious, so as to shore up moral bearing;

sentences.zh: 未退虛鄙，以懲不恪，臣是以猶敢有言。

translations.literal: nor yet dismissed the hollow and base, to punish negligence—therefore your servant still dares to speak."
translations.idiomatic: nor have you yet cleared away the shallow and mean to chastise slack conduct—which is why I still presume to speak."

sentences.zh: 」詔報曰：「舉清遠有禮之臣者，此尤今之要也。

translations.literal: " An edict replied: "To promote ministers who are pure, remote, and courteous—this is especially today's imperative.
translations.idiomatic: The reply edict said: "Raising up principled, courteous men is precisely what the times require most.

sentences.zh: 」乃使玄草詔進之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ordered Fu Xuan to draft the edict and present it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then told Fu Xuan to draft the edict and advance it.

sentences.zh: 玄復上疏曰：

translations.literal: Fu Xuan again submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan submitted another long memorial:

sentences.zh: 書奏，帝下詔曰：「二常侍懇懇於所論，可謂乃心欲佐益時事者也。

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, the emperor issued an edict: "The earnestness with which the two attendants-in-ordinary argued what they discussed may be called hearts bent on aiding and improving current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the paper reached the throne, the emperor issued an edict: "The two Regular Attendants have argued their case with real earnestness; plainly they mean to help set the age to rights.

sentences.zh: 而主者率以常制裁之，豈得不使發憤耶！

translations.literal: Yet those in charge routinely bound them with standing regulations—how could that not stir indignation!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the responsible offices keep trapping them in routine precedent—small wonder they boil with frustration!

sentences.zh: 二常侍所論，或舉其大較而未備其條目，亦可便令作之，然後主者八坐廣共研精。

translations.literal: What the two attendants-in-ordinary discussed sometimes states the general drift without supplying every clause; it may also be ordered produced in full, after which those in charge and the Eight Seats should broadly examine it together.
translations.idiomatic: Their memorial may give the broad outline without every detail; have them expand it into a full draft, then let the relevant departments and the Eight Seats thrash it out together.

sentences.zh: 凡關言於人主，人臣之所至難。

translations.literal: In general, remonstrating with the sovereign is the hardest thing for a minister.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking truth to a sovereign is about the hardest duty a subject can bear.

sentences.zh: 而人主若不能虛心聽納，自古忠臣直士之所慷慨，至使杜口結舌。

translations.literal: Yet if the sovereign cannot listen with an empty mind, since antiquity loyal ministers and upright gentlemen have lamented it in vain, until they sealed their mouths and tied their tongues.
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler will not listen with an open mind, loyal men through the ages have pressed their case until, despairing, they clammed up entirely.

sentences.zh: 每念於此，未嘗不歎息也。

translations.literal: Whenever I think of this, I cannot but sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I think of it, I cannot help sighing.

sentences.zh: 故前詔敢有直言，勿有所距，庶幾得以發懞補過，獲保高位。

translations.literal: Hence the earlier edict dared straight speech with nothing rejected, hoping thereby to expose foolishness and mend faults and preserve high rank.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the earlier edict invited blunt counsel with nothing turned away—so honest mistakes could surface, faults be repaired, and high office kept secure.

sentences.zh: 苟言有偏善，情在忠益，雖文辭有謬誤，言語有失得，皆當曠然恕之。

translations.literal: If words show partial merit and the intent lies in loyal benefit, though the wording errs or the speech slips, all should be forgiven with breadth.
translations.idiomatic: If a statement has something worthwhile in it and the motive is loyal service, then even clumsy wording or a careless phrase ought to be met with generous forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 古人猶不拒誹謗，況皆善意在可採錄乎！

translations.literal: The ancients still did not reject slander—how much more when the good intent is worth recording!
translations.idiomatic: The ancients did not shut their ears even to bitter criticism—how much less should we shut out advice offered in good faith!

sentences.zh: 近者孔晁、綦毋龢皆案以輕慢之罪，所以皆原，欲使四海知區區之朝無諱言之忌也。

translations.literal: Recently Kong Chao and Qi Wu He were both prosecuted for the offense of disrespect; both were therefore pardoned, intending to let the four seas know that this modest court has no taboo against frank speech."
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago Kong Chao and Qi Wu He were charged with disrespect; both were forgiven on purpose, so the empire would see that this court does not fear plain speech."

sentences.zh: 」俄遷侍中。

translations.literal: " Shortly thereafter [Fu Xuan] was promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Fu Xuan was promoted to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 初，玄進皇甫陶，及入而抵，玄以事與陶爭，言喧嘩，為有司所奏，二人竟坐免官。

translations.literal: Earlier, Fu Xuan had recommended Huangfu Tao; once [Tao] entered office they clashed. Fu Xuan quarreled with Tao over affairs, their words noisy; the authorities impeached them, and both were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Fu Xuan had recommended Huangfu Tao; after Tao took office the two were at odds. They quarreled aloud over policy until the authorities impeached them, and both men lost their posts.

sentences.zh: 俄復為御史中丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was again appointed Palace Assistant Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was reappointed Palace Assistant Clerk.

sentences.zh: 時頗有水旱之災，玄復上疏曰：

translations.literal: At that time there were frequent floods and droughts; Fu Xuan again submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: Floods and droughts had become frequent; Fu Xuan once more laid a memorial before the throne:

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「得所陳便宜，言農事得失及水官興廢，又安邊禦胡政事寬猛之宜，申省周備，一二具之，此誠為國大本，當今急務也。

translations.literal: An edict said: "What you have presented as expedient—speaking of farming's gains and losses and the rise and fall of water offices, also border defense against the Hu and whether administration should be lenient or stern—you have laid out thoroughly and prepared every item in order; this is indeed the great foundation of the state and the urgent task of the day.
translations.idiomatic: An edict answered: "The practical measures you cite—agriculture's strengths and failures, which waterworks to keep or abolish, how to secure the frontier against the Hu and calibrate strict versus lenient rule—you have spelled out item by item. These are indeed the state's foundation and the business that cannot wait.

sentences.zh: 如所論皆善，深知乃心，廣思諸宜，動靜以聞也。」

translations.literal: If what you argue is all good, we deeply know your intent; broadly think through every suitable measure and report whether to move or stay."
translations.idiomatic: If your proposals hold up, we credit your sincerity; think through every fitting remedy and keep us informed as circumstances shift."

sentences.zh: 五年，遷太僕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year [of a reign era], he was promoted to Grand Coachman.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to Grand Coachman.

sentences.zh: 時比年不登，羌胡擾邊，詔公卿會議。

translations.literal: Harvests had failed several years running and the Qiang and Hu troubled the borders; an edict convened the dukes and ministers for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Harvests had failed year after year and Qiang and Hu raiders harried the frontier; an edict summoned the highest ministers to council.

sentences.zh: 玄應對所問，陳事切直，雖不盡施行，而常見優容。

translations.literal: Fu Xuan answered what was asked; his statements were bluntly forthright. Though not everything was implemented, he was usually treated with indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan replied to each question in blunt, uncompromising terms. Not every suggestion was adopted, yet the throne generally indulged him.

sentences.zh: 轉司隸校尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Metropolitan Governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Metropolitan Governor.

sentences.zh: 獻皇后崩于弘訓宮，設喪位。

translations.literal: Empress Xian died in the Hongxun Palace; mourning stations were set up.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Xian died in Hongxun Palace, mourning stations were arranged.

sentences.zh: 舊制，司隸於端門外坐，在諸卿上，絕席。

translations.literal: Under old regulations the Metropolitan Governor sat outside the Duan Gate, above the various ministers, on a separate mat.
translations.idiomatic: By longstanding rule the Metropolitan Governor sat outside the Duan Gate above the chief ministers, on his own mat.

sentences.zh: 其入殿，按本品秩在諸卿下，以次坐，不絕席。

translations.literal: When he entered the hall, according to his rank and grade he sat below the various ministers in order, not on a separate mat.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the hall, according to rank he took his place below the ministers in sequence and shared the common seating.

sentences.zh: 而謁者以弘訓宮為殿內，制玄位在卿下。

translations.literal: But the herald took the Hongxun Palace to be "inside the hall" and placed Fu Xuan's seat below the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The court herald treated Hongxun Palace as "within the hall precinct" and assigned Fu Xuan a seat beneath the ministers.

sentences.zh: 玄恚怒，厲聲色而責謁者。

translations.literal: Fu Xuan was furious; with stern voice and face he berated the herald.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan flushed with rage and dressed down the herald in a thundering voice.

sentences.zh: 謁者妄稱尚書所處，玄對百僚而罵尚書以下。

translations.literal: The herald falsely claimed it was the placement decided by the Secretariat; Fu Xuan, facing the hundred officials, reviled the Secretariat downward.
translations.idiomatic: The herald falsely said the Secretariat had fixed the seating; Fu Xuan then berated everyone from the Secretariat downward in front of the full assembly.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞庾純奏玄不敬，玄又自表不以實，坐免官。

translations.literal: Palace Assistant Clerk Yu Chun impeached Fu Xuan for disrespect; Fu Xuan also submitted a self-report that did not match the facts; he was dismissed on account of this.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Assistant Clerk Yu Chun impeached Fu Xuan for lèse-majesté; Fu Xuan's own statement did not match the facts, and he was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 然玄天性峻急，不能有所容；

translations.literal: Yet Fu Xuan's nature was harsh and impatient; he could tolerate nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Fu Xuan's temperament was harsh and impatient—he suffered no opposition.

sentences.zh: 每有奏劾，或值日暮，捧白簡，整簪帶，竦踴不寐，坐而待旦。

translations.literal: Whenever he submitted an impeachment—sometimes when dusk fell—he would grasp his white baton, straighten cap and sash, stand taut and sleepless, sit and wait for dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he framed an impeachment—even if night was falling—he would clutch his white accusation slip, straighten cap and sash, sit bolt upright without sleeping, and wait for dawn.

sentences.zh: 於是貴遊懾伏，臺閣生風。

translations.literal: Thereupon the noble circles trembled and submitted; the terraces and galleries caught a stern wind.
translations.idiomatic: The great families quailed; a chill wind seemed to blow through the ministries.

sentences.zh: 尋卒于家，時年六十二，諡曰剛。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died at home, aged sixty-two; his posthumous title was Gang ("Relentless").
translations.idiomatic: He died at home not long after, aged sixty-two, with the posthumous epithet Gang, "Relentless."

sentences.zh: 玄少時避難於河內，專心誦學，後雖顯貴，而著述不廢。

translations.literal: In youth Fu Xuan had fled trouble to Henei and devoted himself to study; though later eminent, he never ceased writing.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Fu Xuan had taken refuge in Henei and immersed himself in scholarship; though he rose to high rank, he never stopped writing.

sentences.zh: 撰論經國九流及三史故事，評斷得失，各為區例，名為《傅子》，為內、外、中篇，凡有四部、六錄，合百四十首，數十萬言，並文集百餘卷行於世。

translations.literal: He composed treatises on governing the state, the nine currents, and anecdotes from the three histories, judging gain and loss and setting each in its own category; the work was titled Master Fu, in inner, outer, and middle sections—four divisions and six registers in all, one hundred forty pieces, several hundred thousand characters, together with over a hundred fascicles of collected writings, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote on ordering the realm, the nine schools of thought, and episodes drawn from the three histories, weighing right and wrong and sorting each topic—compiled as the Master Fu in inner, outer, and middle books: four parts, six registers, one hundred forty chapters and several hundred thousand characters, plus another hundred-odd fascicles of collected prose that circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 玄初作內篇成，子咸以示司空王沈。

translations.literal: When Fu Xuan first finished the inner sections, his son Xian showed them to Minister of Works Wang Shen.
translations.idiomatic: When the inner books were complete, his son Fu Xian showed them to Wang Shen, the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 沈與玄書曰：「省足下所著書，言富理濟，經綸政體，存重儒教，足以塞楊、墨之流遁，齊孫、孟于往代。

translations.literal: Shen wrote to Fu Xuan: "I have reviewed what you have written: the words are rich and the principles sustain governance; it orders the body politic and esteems Confucian teaching—enough to block the evasions of Yang [Zhu] and Mo [Di] and to rank Sun [Zi] and Mencius with past ages.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen wrote to him: "I have read your work: it is ample in argument and sound on policy; it maps the machinery of government and honors Confucian teaching—enough to shut down the evasions of Yang Zhu and Mozi and to set Sunzi and Mencius beside the worthies of old.

sentences.zh: 每開卷，未嘗不歎息也。

translations.literal: Whenever I open the fascicle, I cannot but sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Every time I open the manuscript I cannot help sighing.

sentences.zh: 『不見賈生，自以過之，乃今不及』，信矣！」

translations.literal: "I did not see Jia Yi; I thought I surpassed him—now I am not equal"—true indeed!"
translations.idiomatic: "'Without meeting Jia Yi I fancied myself his better—now I see I am not.' That verdict was just!"

sentences.zh: 其後追封清泉侯。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Qingquan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Qingquan.

sentences.zh: 子咸嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xian inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu Xian inherited the title.

translations.literal: Equals sign.
translations.idiomatic: The transmitted text here inserts a stray mark from the typesetting source.

sentences.zh: 子咸

translations.literal: "Zi" Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian.

sentences.zh: 咸字長虞，剛簡有大節。

translations.literal: His courtesy name was Changyu; he was stern and plain and had great integrity.
translations.idiomatic: His courtesy name was Changyu; he was austere, upright, and possessed of strong moral principle.

sentences.zh: 風格峻整，識性明悟，疾惡如仇，推賢樂善，常慕季文子、仲山甫之志。

translations.literal: His manner was severe and ordered; his discernment was sharp and clear; he hated evil as an enemy, promoted the worthy and delighted in goodness, and always admired the aims of Ji Wenzi and Zhong Shanfu.
translations.idiomatic: His deportment was stern and disciplined, his judgment lucid; he hated wickedness as he would a personal foe, lifted up the worthy, rejoiced in goodness, and modeled himself on Ji Wenzi and Zhong Shanfu.

sentences.zh: 好屬文論，雖綺麗不足，而言成規鑒。

translations.literal: He liked to compose essays; though they lacked ornate beauty, his words became models and mirrors.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to write essays; they were never ornate, yet every line carried the force of a standard and a mirror.

sentences.zh: 潁川庾純常歎曰：「長虞之文近乎詩人之作矣！」

translations.literal: Yu Chun of Yingchuan often sighed: "Changyu's writings are close to the work of poets!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun of Yingchuan used to exclaim, "Changyu's prose stands almost with the poets!"

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，襲父爵，拜太子洗馬，累遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xianning era he inherited his father's noble rank, was appointed Horsewasher to the heir apparent, and was promoted step by step to Right Assistant to the Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianning era he inherited his father's noble rank, became Horsewasher to the heir apparent, and rose through several posts to Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 出為冀州刺史，繼母杜氏不肯隨咸之官，自表解職。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Ji Province; his stepmother, Lady Du, refused to follow Xian to his post, so he submitted a memorial requesting release from office.
translations.idiomatic: When he went out as Inspector of Ji Province, his stepmother Lady Du refused to travel with him; he therefore asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 三旬之間，遷司徒左長史。

translations.literal: Within thirty days he was promoted to Left Senior Clerk to the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Within thirty days he was promoted to Senior Clerk on the left of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 時帝留心政事，詔訪朝臣政之損益。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor attended to government affairs and issued an edict asking court ministers about what harmed or helped administration.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then actively engaged with governance and ordered his ministers to say what helped or hurt statecraft.

sentences.zh: 咸上言曰：「陛下處至尊之位，而修布衣之事，親覽萬機，勞心日昃。

translations.literal: Xian submitted: "Your Majesty occupies the loftiest station yet conducts the business of a commoner, personally reviewing the myriad threads of policy and toiling from sunrise past noon.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian replied: "You hold the highest throne yet busy yourself like a common clerk, personally tending every thread of government from dawn past midday.

sentences.zh: 在昔帝王，躬自菲薄，以利天下，未有逾陛下也。

translations.literal: Among emperors of old who humbled themselves to benefit All under Heaven, none has exceeded Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Among past emperors who tightened their belts for the realm's sake, none has outdone you.

sentences.zh: 然泰始開元以暨於今，十有五年矣。

translations.literal: Yet from the opening of the Taishi era until now, fifteen years have passed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the founding Taishi era to the present, fifteen years have passed.

sentences.zh: 而軍國未豐，百姓不贍，一歲不登便有菜色者，誠由官眾事殷，復除猥濫，蠶食者多而親農者少也。

translations.literal: Yet the army and state are not abundant and the hundred surnames lack surplus; if one year's harvest fails there are faces showing hunger—this is truly because offices are many and business heavy, exemptions are reckless and excessive, those who nibble away are many while those who personally farm are few.
translations.idiomatic: Still the army and treasury run thin and the common people have no margin; one bad harvest and faces turn hungry—because offices multiply and paperwork swells, tax favors are handed out indiscriminately, parasites abound, and few tend the soil themselves.

sentences.zh: 臣以頑疏，謬忝近職，每見聖詔以百姓饑饉為慮，無能雲補，伏用慚恧，敢不自竭，以對天問。

translations.literal: Your servant is dull and coarse and wrongly holds a post close to the throne; whenever I see a sagely edict worrying over the people's famine, I have no way to help and bow my head in shame; I dare not fail to exhaust myself in answering Heaven's question.
translations.idiomatic: I am thick-witted and unworthy of the place near you; whenever an edict voices concern over famine I have nothing to offer and hang my head in shame—yet I dare answer your inquiry with all I have.

sentences.zh: 舊都督有四，今並監軍，乃盈於十。

translations.literal: Formerly there were four area commanders-in-chief; now together with army supervisors they exceed ten.
translations.idiomatic: There used to be four regional commanders-in-chief; now, counting army supervisors, there are more than ten.

sentences.zh: 夏禹敷土，分為九州，今之刺史，幾向一倍。

translations.literal: Yu of Xia spread the soil and divided it into nine provinces; today's regional governors are nearly double that number.
translations.idiomatic: Yu smeared the flood-soaked earth and carved nine provinces; today's inspectors are nearly twice as many.

sentences.zh: 戶口比漢十分之一，而置郡縣更多。

translations.literal: Registered households are one-tenth of the Han, yet commanderies and counties are even more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Registered households are barely one-tenth of Han levels, yet we maintain even more commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 空校牙門，無益宿衛，而虛立軍府，動有百數。

translations.literal: Empty camps at the Ya gates bring no benefit to night defense, yet hollow army headquarters are set up by the hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Idle detachments at the Ya gates do nothing for palace security, yet phantom army offices sprawl by the hundreds.

sentences.zh: 五等諸侯，復坐置官屬。

translations.literal: The nobles of the five ranks again sit and establish office staffs.
translations.idiomatic: The ranked nobles again maintain full administrative retinues.

sentences.zh: 諸所寵給，皆生於百姓。

translations.literal: All they are favored with is born from the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Every stipend they enjoy is wrung from common households.

sentences.zh: 一夫不農，有受其饑，今之不農，不可勝計。

translations.literal: If one man does not farm, someone goes hungry; today those who do not farm cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: When one man leaves the plough someone goes hungry; today the idle cannot even be counted.

sentences.zh: 縱使五稼普收，僅足相接；

translations.literal: Even if the five grains all ripened in one season, it would barely suffice to meet needs;
translations.idiomatic: Even if every crop ripened well it would only barely cover consumption;

sentences.zh: 暫有災患，便不繼贍。

translations.literal: the moment there is disaster or trouble, there is no surplus to draw on.
translations.idiomatic: the instant calamity strikes there is nothing in reserve.

sentences.zh: 以為當今之急，先並官省事，靜事息役，上下用心，惟農是務也。」

translations.literal: Your servant holds that the urgency of the moment is first to merge offices and cut affairs, quiet affairs and rest labor, so that high and low set their hearts on nothing but farming."
translations.idiomatic: I believe the pressing task is to consolidate offices, cut redundant duties, still disturbances, and ease corvée so that everyone from the throne down fixes mind and muscle on farming alone."

sentences.zh: 咸在位多所執正。

translations.literal: While in office Xian often upheld what was correct.
translations.idiomatic: In office Fu Xian repeatedly stood his ground on what was right.

sentences.zh: 豫州大中正夏侯駿上言，魯國小中正、司空司馬孔毓，四移病所，不能接賓，求以尚書郎曹馥代毓，旬日復上毓為中正。

translations.literal: The senior provincial appraiser of Yu Province, Xiahou Jun, submitted: the junior appraiser of Lu, Kong Yu, Vice Minister of Works to the Minister of Works, had shifted his sick-leave location four times and could not receive guests; he asked that Gentleman of the Masters of Writing Cao Fu replace Yu; ten days later he again submitted Yu as appraiser.
translations.idiomatic: The Greater Provincial Evaluator for Yu, Xiahou Jun, reported that Kong Yu—junior evaluator for Lu and secretary to the Minister of Works—had changed his sick-leave residence four times and could no longer receive visitors; Jun asked to replace him with Cao Fu of the Masters of Writing, then ten days later nominated Kong Yu again.

sentences.zh: 司徒三卻，駿故據正。

translations.literal: The Minister of Education thrice rejected it; Jun therefore insisted on what was correct.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education rejected the paperwork three times running; Jun dug in on what he saw as proper procedure.

sentences.zh: 咸以駿與奪惟意，乃奏免駿大中正。

translations.literal: Xian held that Jun made appointments and dismissals as he pleased and therefore memorialized to dismiss Jun as senior appraiser.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian argued that Jun was handing out posts on whim and memorialized to strip him of the Greater Evaluator title.

sentences.zh: 司徒魏舒，駿之姻屬，屢卻不署，咸據正甚苦。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Wei Shu, related by marriage to Jun, repeatedly rejected and would not sign; Xian pressed what was correct with bitter persistence.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wei Shu—Jun's kinsman by marriage—kept refusing to countersign; Fu Xian hammered away at procedural justice.

sentences.zh: 舒終不從，咸遂獨上。

translations.literal: Shu in the end did not comply; Xian therefore submitted alone.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu still would not yield, so Fu Xian forwarded the memorial on his own.

sentences.zh: 舒奏咸激訕不直，詔轉咸為車騎司馬。

translations.literal: Shu memorialized that Xian was provocative and insincere; an edict transferred Xian to Chief Clerk to the Cavalry-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu accused Fu Xian of inflammatory disrespect; an edict reassigned him as Chief Clerk to the Chief Commandant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 咸以世俗奢侈，又上書曰：「臣以為穀帛難生，而用之不節，無緣不匱。

translations.literal: Xian, because customs in the world were extravagant, again submitted: "Your servant holds that grain and silk are hard to produce; if use is not restrained, there is no way not to run short.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing society sunk in extravagance, Fu Xian submitted again: "Grain and cloth do not come easily; spend without restraint and shortage follows inevitably.

sentences.zh: 故先王之化天下，食肉衣帛，皆有其制。

translations.literal: Thus when former kings transformed All under Heaven, eating meat and wearing silk each had its regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings who civilized the realm set strict rules even for eating meat and wearing silk.

sentences.zh: 竊謂奢侈之費，甚於天災。

translations.literal: Your servant privately holds that the cost of extravagance exceeds natural disaster.
translations.idiomatic: I would argue that waste costs more than flood or drought.

sentences.zh: 古者堯有茅茨，今之百姓競豐其屋。

translations.literal: In antiquity Yao had a thatched roof; today the hundred surnames compete to make their houses lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's hall was thatched straw; the common people now outdo one another in grand houses.

sentences.zh: 古者臣無玉食，今之賈豎皆厭粱肉。

translations.literal: In antiquity ministers had no jade food; today peddlers and grooms are sated with millet and meat.
translations.idiomatic: Once, only the great ate off jade; today even peddlers turn up their noses at fine millet and meat.

sentences.zh: 古者后妃乃有殊飾，今之婢妾被服綾羅。

translations.literal: In antiquity empresses and consorts alone had special ornaments; today maids and concubines are robed in damask and gauze.
translations.idiomatic: In old days only palace ladies wore rare finery; now every chambermaid swathes herself in silk.

sentences.zh: 古者大夫乃不徒行，今之賤隸乘輕驅肥。

translations.literal: In antiquity great officers did not walk afoot; today base bond-servants ride light carriages and drive fat horses.
translations.idiomatic: Once, ministers did not go on foot; now the lowliest grooms trot out in light chars and plump ponies.

sentences.zh: 古者人稠地狹而有儲蓄，由於節也；

translations.literal: In antiquity the people were dense and the land narrow yet there were stores, because of restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity was crowded and cramped, yet granaries held surplus—because people practiced restraint.

sentences.zh: 今者土廣人稀而患不足，由於奢也。

translations.literal: Today the soil is broad and people sparse yet there is worry about insufficiency, because of extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Now land lies wide and population thin, yet want persists—because extravagance drains everything.

sentences.zh: 欲時之儉，當詰其奢；

translations.literal: Desiring frugality for the age, one ought to call extravagance to account;
translations.idiomatic: If we want an age of thrift, we must confront waste head-on;

sentences.zh: 奢不見詰，轉相高尚。

translations.literal: if extravagance is not called to account, they vie to esteem one another higher.
translations.idiomatic: left unchecked, ostentation becomes a contest of one-upmanship.

sentences.zh: 昔毛玠為吏部尚書，時無敢好衣美食者。

translations.literal: Formerly Mao Jie was Minister of the Masters of Writing for personnel; at the time none dared fine clothes or rich food.
translations.idiomatic: When Mao Jie ran the Ministry of Personnel, no one dared dress richly or dine sumptuously.

sentences.zh: 魏武帝歎曰：『孤之法不如毛尚書。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei sighed: "My laws do not match Minister Mao's."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao once sighed, "My statutes cannot compare with Minister Mao's discipline."

sentences.zh: 』令使諸部用心，各如毛玠，風俗之移，在不難矣。

translations.literal: " Order the departments to apply themselves each like Mao Jie; shifting custom would not be difficult."
translations.idiomatic: "If every bureau applied Mao Jie's zeal, reforming morals would be easy."

sentences.zh: 」又議移縣獄於郡及二社應立，朝廷從之。

translations.literal: " He also debated moving county prisons to the commandery and that the two shrines of soil and grain ought to be established; the court approved.
translations.idiomatic: He further urged relocating county jails to commandery seats and erecting the twin altars to soil and grain; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted Assistant Director on the left of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 惠帝即位，楊駿輔政。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui ascended the throne, Yang Jun directed the government.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui took the throne with Yang Jun steering policy.

sentences.zh: 咸言於駿曰：「事與世變，禮隨時宜，諒暗之不行尚矣。

translations.literal: Xian spoke to Jun, saying: "Affairs change with the age; ritual follows what is timely—mourning in seclusion not observed has long been the case.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian told Yang Jun: "Times change, and ritual must keep pace—full palace seclusion during mourning has long since ceased to be workable.

sentences.zh: 由世道彌薄，權不可假，故雖斬焉在疚，而躬覽萬機也。

translations.literal: Because the age's Way grows thinner, authority cannot be lent away; therefore though worn with mourning grief one personally oversees the myriad threads.
translations.idiomatic: As public morality thins, power cannot be delegated; even wrapped in mourning one must still grasp every lever of rule oneself.

sentences.zh: 逮至漢文，以天下體大，服重難久，遂制既葬而除。

translations.literal: Down to Emperor Wen of Han, because All under Heaven's frame was large and heavy mourning could not long endure, therefore he established dismissal upon completing burial.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han faced an empire too vast for endless sackcloth; he settled on shedding mourning garments once burial ended.

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝雖大孝蒸蒸，亦從時釋服，制心喪三年，至於萬機之事，則有不遑。

translations.literal: Though Emperor Wu of our dynasty [Sima Yan] was steeped in the utmost filial devotion, he likewise followed the times in releasing mourning garments, regulating inner mourning three years—as for the myriad threads of policy, there were matters he could not tarry on.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu showed towering filial piety, yet he too shortened formal mourning to suit the age—three years of restrained grief—because government business would not wait.

sentences.zh: 今聖上欲委政於公，諒暗自居，此雖謙讓之心，而天下未以為善。

translations.literal: Now the sagely sovereign wishes to entrust government to Your Grace and dwell in seclusion himself—though this is a mind of modest yielding, All under Heaven does not deem it good.
translations.idiomatic: Now the sovereign proposes to hand you the reins while he retires into mourning withdrawal—it sounds humble, but the realm reads it as wrongheaded.

sentences.zh: 天下未以為善者，以億兆顒顒，戴仰宸極，聽於冢宰，懼天光有蔽。

translations.literal: The reason All under Heaven does not deem it good is that the myriad hosts crane upward, look up to the polar throne, listen to the chief minister, and fear the celestial radiance may be blocked.
translations.idiomatic: They crane their necks toward the throne; they dread hearing policy filter only through a chief minister while the emperor's light stays hidden.

sentences.zh: 人心既已若此，而明公處之固未為易也。

translations.literal: Human hearts being already thus, for Your notable lordship to manage it is surely not easy.
translations.idiomatic: With opinion running this way, Your Honor walks an impossible tightrope.

sentences.zh: 竊謂山陵之事既畢，明公當思隆替之宜。

translations.literal: Your servant privately considers that once the mausoleum business is finished, Your Grace ought to ponder what suits rising or declining fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Once the late emperor rests in his tomb, you must weigh what consolidation—or collapse—requires.

sentences.zh: 周公聖人，猶不免謗。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou was a sage; still he did not escape slander.
translations.idiomatic: Even the Duke of Zhou, a sage, faced backbiters.

sentences.zh: 以此推之，周公之任既未易而處，況聖上春秋非成王之年乎！

translations.literal: By this reasoning, the Duke of Zhou's charge was already not easy to occupy—how much less when the sagely sovereign's years are not the age of King Cheng!
translations.idiomatic: If holding the Duke of Zhou's mandate was treacherous even then, think how much harder now—the emperor is no child-king Cheng.

sentences.zh: 得意忘言，言未易盡。

translations.literal: When meaning is grasped words are forgotten—words are not easy to exhaust.
translations.idiomatic: Meaning, once caught, outruns words—language cannot capture everything.

sentences.zh: 苟明公有以察其悾款，言豈在多。

translations.literal: If Your notable lordship has means to perceive sincere earnestness, words need not be many.
translations.idiomatic: If you read sincerity in my intent, I need not speak at length.

sentences.zh: 」時司隸荀愷從兄喪，自表赴哀，詔聽之而未下，愷乃造駿。

translations.literal: " At that time the Metropolitan Governor Xun Kai [mourning] his elder cousin's death, personally memorialized to hurry to mourning; an edict permitted it but had not yet issued—Kai therefore visited Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Metropolitan Governor Xun Kai had lost an elder cousin and petitioned to rush to the funeral—permission was promised but the edict had not dropped—yet Kai presented himself at Yang Jun's door anyway.

sentences.zh: 咸因奏曰：「死喪之戚，兄弟孔懷。

translations.literal: Xian therefore memorialized: "The grief of death and mourning—between brothers there is deep pity.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian seized on it: "The ache of bereavement hits brothers hardest.

sentences.zh: 同堂亡隕，方在信宿，聖恩矜憫，聽使臨喪。

translations.literal: A hall-fellow has just died—barely two nights—sagely grace sympathizes and permits attendance at mourning.
translations.idiomatic: A cousin has barely lain cold two nights; imperial mercy allows you to mourn him.

sentences.zh: 詔未下而便以行造，急諂媚之敬，無友于之情。

translations.literal: Before the edict had issued yet they hastened to call—the urgency is obsequious respect—there is no feeling of brotherhood.
translations.idiomatic: But Kai rushed to Yang Jun's chambers before the paper arrived—urgent flattery, not fraternal feeling.

sentences.zh: 宜加顯貶，以隆風教。

translations.literal: They ought to suffer conspicuous demotion in order to elevate customs and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He deserves public demotion to reinforce ethical teaching.

sentences.zh: 」帝以駿管朝政，有詔不問，駿甚憚之。

translations.literal: " The emperor because Jun managed court government issued an edict not to investigate—Jun greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yang Jun still controlled the court, the emperor brushed off Fu Xian's charge—Yang Jun learned to fear him.

sentences.zh: 咸復與駿箋諷切之，駿意稍折，漸以不平。

translations.literal: Xian again sent Jun a note sharply criticizing; Jun's attitude bent slightly and gradually grew resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian followed with a biting letter; Yang Jun yielded a little but nursed growing resentment.

sentences.zh: 由是欲出為京兆、弘農太守，駿甥李斌說駿，不宜斥出正人，乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon [Jun] wished to send him out as Governor of Jingzhao or Hongnong—Jun's nephew Li Bin persuaded Jun that upright men ought not be expelled; therefore it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun tried to exile him as governor of Jingzhao or Hongnong until nephew Li Bin argued that banishing honest ministers would backfire.

sentences.zh: 駿弟濟素與咸善，與咸書曰：「江海之流混混，故能成其深廣也。

translations.literal: Jun's younger brother Ji was always friendly with Xian; he wrote Xian, saying: "The rivers and seas flow turbid and rolling—therefore they achieve depth and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun's brother Yang Ji, who was fond of Fu Xian, wrote: "Great rivers stay broad because they tolerate muddy torrents.

sentences.zh: 天下大器，非可稍了，而相觀每事欲了。

translations.literal: All under Heaven is a great vessel—not something one can finish slightly—and mutual observation desires each matter finished.
translations.idiomatic: The empire is too vast to tidy up quickly; yet everyone insists every loose end be tied at once.

sentences.zh: 生子癡，了官事，官事未易了也。

translations.literal: Bear sons foolish; finish official business—official business is not easy to finish.
translations.idiomatic: They say blockheads solve bureaucracy—yet bureaucracy never stays solved.

sentences.zh: 了事正作癡，復為快耳！

translations.literal: Finishing affairs is precisely being foolish—again it becomes mere pleasure!
translations.idiomatic: Trying to 'finish' everything is itself a fool's game—and only sparks fresh trouble.

sentences.zh: 左丞總司天臺，維正八坐，此未易居。

translations.literal: The Left Assistant Director oversees the celestial terrace and ties upright the Eight Seats—this is not easy to occupy.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Assistant Director anchors the High Terrace and keeps the Eight Seats honest—no easy chair.

sentences.zh: 以君盡性而處未易居之任，益不易也。

translations.literal: With your exhausting nature occupying a hard-to-occupy charge, it is yet more not easy.
translations.idiomatic: You give everything to hold an office that breaks lesser men—that makes the burden heavier.

sentences.zh: 想慮破頭，故具有白。

translations.literal: I suppose worry splits the skull—therefore I set this out fully.
translations.idiomatic: I imagine your skull aches—I spell this out bluntly.

sentences.zh: 」咸答曰：「衛公云酒色之殺人，此甚於作直。

translations.literal: " Xian replied: "Lord Wei states that wine and sex kill men—this surpasses practicing forthrightness.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian answered: "Wei Jun once said wine and lust kill faster than blunt counsel.

sentences.zh: 坐酒色死，人不為悔。

translations.literal: Die sitting with wine and sex—people do not regret it.
translations.idiomatic: Men die of winebeds without regret.

sentences.zh: 逆畏以直致禍，此由心不直正，欲以苟且為明哲耳！

translations.literal: Contrarily fearing that forthrightness brings disaster—this comes from the heart not being straight and correct, wishing to take temporizing as enlightened wisdom!
translations.idiomatic: When people dread blunt speech as dangerous, it is because their hearts are crooked and they mistake cowardice for wisdom.

sentences.zh: 自古以直致禍者，當自矯枉過直，或不忠允，欲以亢厲為聲，故致忿耳。

translations.literal: Since antiquity those who brought disaster through forthrightness either corrected excess by excess or failed loyalty and sincerity, wishing to take shrill severity as reputation—therefore they stirred resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Those historically punished for candor either overcorrected or lacked honest loyalty—raising their voices only for fame—and earned resentment.

sentences.zh: 安有空空為忠益，而當見疾乎！

translations.literal: How could empty loyalty meant for benefit yet meet hatred!
translations.idiomatic: How could sincere counsel meant to help draw hatred?

sentences.zh: 」居無何，駿誅。

translations.literal: " Before long Yang Jun was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yang Jun fell and died.

sentences.zh: 咸轉為太子中庶子，遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: Xian was transferred to serve as Palace Clerk to the heir apparent and promoted Palace Assistant Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian moved to Palace Clerk to the heir apparent, then rose to Palace Assistant Clerk.

sentences.zh: 時太宰、汝南王亮輔政，咸致書曰：咸以為太甲、成王年在蒙幼，故有伊、周之事。聖人且猶不免疑，況臣既不聖，王非孺子，而可以行伊、周之事乎！上在諒暗，聽於冢宰，而楊駿無狀，便作伊、周，自為居天下之安，所以至死。其罪既不可勝，亦是殿下所見。駿之見討，發自天聰，孟觀、李肇與知密旨耳。至於論功，當歸美於上。觀等已數千戶縣侯，聖上以駿死莫不欣悅，故論功寧厚，以敘其歡心。此群下所宜以實裁量，而遂扇動，東安封王，孟、李郡公，余侯伯子男，既妄有加，復又三等超遷。此之熏赫，震動天地，自古以來，封賞未有若此者也。無功而厚賞，莫不樂國有禍，禍起當復有大功也。人而樂禍，其可極乎！作此者，皆由東安公。謂殿下至止，當有以正之。正之以道，眾亦何所怒乎！眾之所怒，在於不平耳。而今皆更倍論，莫不失望。咸之愚冗，不惟失望而已，竊以為憂。又討駿之時，殿下在外，實所不綜。今欲委重，故令殿下論功。論功之事，實未易可處，莫若坐觀得失，有居正之事宜也。

translations.literal: At the time the Grand Mentor, Prince Liang of Runan, directed the government; Fu Xian sent him a letter saying: Fu Xian considered that Taijia and the King of Cheng were still in infancy and ignorance; hence there were the deeds of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou. Even sages still did not escape suspicion—how much less when your servant is no sage and the king is no child, yet one could enact the deeds of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou! While the sovereign was in the mourning hut listening to the chief minister, Yang Jun behaved without propriety yet posed as Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, settling himself in possession of All under Heaven's security—therefore unto death. His guilt already admits no reckoning, and it is also what Your Highness witnessed. Yang Jun's being punished arose from Heaven's keen insight—only Meng Guan and Li Zhao knew the secret edict. As for judging merit, credit ought to return praise to the sovereign. Meng and his fellows already held county marquisates of several thousand households; because the sagely sovereign rejoiced at Yang Jun's death he judged merit generously to settle their satisfaction—this the hosts of officials ought to measure according to reality—yet they stirred excitement: the Prince of Dong'an was enfeoffed as king, Meng and Li were made dukes of commanderies, the remainder earls, marquises, earls, viscounts, baronets—recklessly promoted and moreover vaulted three grades beyond rank. Such blazing glory shook Heaven and Earth; since antiquity enfeoffments and rewards have never been like this. Without merit yet thick rewards—everyone rejoices should the state suffer calamity; when calamity arises there must again be great merit to seize. If men rejoice in calamity, how can it be brought to an end! Those who did this all stemmed from Duke Dong'an. Your servant thought when Your Highness arrived there ought to be correction of it; correcting it by the Way—why would the multitude rage? What the multitude rage at lies in unfairness—yet now everyone doubles past assessments and none fail to be disappointed. Fu Xian's stupidity and mediocrity—not only disappointment—your servant privately finds it worrisome. Again when Yang Jun was punished Your Highness was outside and truly did not oversee it; now wishing to entrust weight therefore ordered Your Highness to judge merit—the matter of judging merit is truly not easy to handle—better to sit and observe gain and loss; there is appropriateness in holding to rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: While Grand Mentor Sima Liang, Prince of Runan, directed policy, Fu Xian laid before him a long letter. Fu Xian argued that Taijia and the boy King of Cheng had still been infants—which alone justified Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou stepping in—and even those paragons drew suspicion. How could lesser ministers serving an adult sovereign pretend to replay that drama? During the mourning silence the court listened to its steward; Yang Jun, utterly unqualified, styled himself another Yi Yin or Duke of Zhou and acted as though he owned the realm—small wonder he died for it. His crimes overflow reckoning, as Your Highness saw. Heaven itself uncovered Yang Jun; only Meng Guan and Li Zhao knew the sealed orders beforehand. Reward for the coup belonged with the throne: Meng and his fellows already held thousand-household county marquisates, and because the court rejoiced at Yang Jun's fall the emperor deliberately showered them with honors to acknowledge their pleasure—something ministers should have weighed soberly. Instead the court erupted: the Prince of Dong'an became a king, Meng and Li jumped to commandery dukedoms, others clawed through noble ranks without merit and skipped three grades beyond precedent. Never had rewards blazed so high or shaken Heaven and earth so violently. Lavish gifts without merit teach everyone to welcome state catastrophe—calamity becomes another chance to steal merit. When men cheer disaster, where does it stop? Duke Dong'an engineered it all. Your servant expected Your Highness, on arriving, to set things straight; straighten them by principle and the crowd would have nothing to resent—they resent injustice. Yet now every calculation doubles past excess and hope collapses everywhere. Fu Xian is dull-witted; he feels not mere disappointment but dread. When Yang Jun fell Your Highness was abroad and bore no part in planning; now the court wants to lean on you and has ordered you to parcel out merit. That is an almost impossible mandate. Better withdraw, watch how profit and loss unfold, and uphold rectitude from the margins.

sentences.zh: 咸復以亮輔政專權，又諫曰：「楊駿有震主之威，委任親戚，此天下所以喧嘩。

translations.literal: Xian again because Liang dominated government remonstrated, saying: "Yang Jun had the awe that shakes the sovereign; he entrusted kin—this is why All under Heaven clamored.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian turned next to Sima Liang's monopoly on power: "Yang Jun wielded ministerial awe and stuffed offices with kin—that is why the realm boiled.

sentences.zh: 今之處重，宜反此失。

translations.literal: Today's occupying weight ought to reverse this fault.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone holding such authority now must invert that mistake.

sentences.zh: 謂宜靜默頤神，有大得失，乃維持之；

translations.literal: Your servant considers it fitting to keep silent and nourish spirit; when there are great gains or losses, then uphold them;
translations.idiomatic: Stay quiet, husband your strength; intervene only on grave gains or losses;

sentences.zh: 自非大事，一皆抑遣。

translations.literal: if not great matters, altogether suppress and dispatch away.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise brush lesser business aside.

sentences.zh: 比四造詣，及經過尊門，冠蓋車馬，填塞街衢，此之翕習，既宜弭息。

translations.literal: Recently four times visiting and passing Your honorable gate, caps and canopies, carriages and horses, stuffed the streets—such clamorous habit ought already to be stilled.
translations.idiomatic: Lately each visit chokes your avenue with coaches and retainers—this ostentatious habit must end.

sentences.zh: 又夏侯長容奉使為先帝請命，祈禱無感，先帝崩背，宜自咎責，而自求請命之勞，而公以為少府。

translations.literal: Again Changrong of Xiahou was dispatched on mission to plead life for the late emperor; prayers went unanswered; the late emperor passed—he ought to blame himself, yet he seeks credit for the mission's labor, while Your Grace appointed him Supervisor of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Changrong carried prayers for the late emperor's recovery; Heaven did not listen and the emperor died—Changrong should carry guilt, yet he trumpets his embassy while you reward him as Palace Provisioner.

sentences.zh: 私竊之論，雲長容則公之姻，故至於此。

translations.literal: Private humble opinion states that Changrong is Your Grace's marriage kin—therefore it reached this.
translations.idiomatic: Whispers say Changrong is your in-law—that explains the favor.

sentences.zh: 一犬吠形，群犬吠聲，懼於群吠，遂至叵聽也。

translations.literal: One dog barks at a shape; a pack of dogs bark at the sound—fearing the pack's barking, listening becomes unbearable.
translations.idiomatic: One dog snaps at a shadow and the pack joins—hearing that chorus grows unbearable.

sentences.zh: 咸之為人，不能面從而有後言。

translations.literal: As for Xian's being a person—he cannot agree to your face yet have words behind.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian cannot nod yes to your face and mutter behind your back.

sentences.zh: 嘗觸楊駿，幾為身禍；

translations.literal: Once he offended Yang Jun—almost brought bodily disaster;
translations.idiomatic: He once crossed Yang Jun and nearly paid with his life;

sentences.zh: 況于殿下，而當有惜！

translations.literal: how much more toward Your Highness—and ought there be sparing!
translations.idiomatic: how much less should he pull punches with Your Highness?

sentences.zh: 往從駕，殿下見語：『卿不識韓非逆鱗之言耶，而欻摩天子逆鱗！

translations.literal: Formerly attending the imperial escort, Your Highness spoke to him: "Do you not know Han Fei's words on the inverted scales—yet suddenly you stroke the Son of Heaven's inverted scales!
translations.idiomatic: Once on an outing you told him, "Have you forgotten Han Fei's lesson on the ruler's reverse scales—yet you keep rubbing the emperor the wrong way!"

sentences.zh: 』自知所陳，誠𬱃𬱃觸猛獸之須耳。

translations.literal: " Your servant knows what he has stated—in truth earnestly plucking the fierce beast's whiskers.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian answered: "I know—I am truly tugging the tiger's whiskers.

sentences.zh: 所以敢言，庶殿下當識其不勝區區。

translations.literal: The reason your servant dares speak—hopefully Your Highness will recognize his inability to overcome petty sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: I speak anyway, hoping you recognize how badly my heart drives me.

sentences.zh: 前摩天子逆鱗，欲以盡忠；

translations.literal: Formerly stroking the Son of Heaven's inverted scales—wished thereby to exhaust loyalty;
translations.idiomatic: Before, I brushed the emperor's scales to prove loyalty;

sentences.zh: 今觸猛獸之須，非欲為惡，必將以此見恕。

translations.literal: now plucking the fierce beast's whiskers—not wishing to do evil—surely will by this meet forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: now I tug yours—not from malice—and trust you will forgive it.

sentences.zh: 」亮不納。

translations.literal: " Liang did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Liang brushed him aside.

sentences.zh: 長容者，夏侯駿也。

translations.literal: Changrong is Xiahou Jun.
translations.idiomatic: "Changrong" means Xiahou Jun.

sentences.zh: 會丙寅，詔群僚舉郡縣之職以補內官。

translations.literal: On the bingyin day an edict ordered the host of officials to nominate commandery and county posts to fill inner offices.
translations.idiomatic: On a bingyin day the court ordered ministers to recommend local posts to staff the inner bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 咸復上書曰：

translations.literal: Xian again submitted:
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian presented another memorial:

sentences.zh: 咸再為本郡中正，遭繼母憂去官。

translations.literal: Xian twice served as appraiser of his home commandery; encountering stepmother mourning he left office.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he served as provincial evaluator for his native commandery; mourning his stepmother forced him out.

sentences.zh: 頃之，起以議郎，長兼司隸校尉。

translations.literal: Shortly he was raised as Consultant and concurrently Metropolitan Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as a Consultant and concurrently Metropolitan Governor.

sentences.zh: 咸前後固辭，不聽，敕使者就拜，咸復送還印綬。

translations.literal: Xian repeatedly declined firmly; [the court] did not listen—ordered envoys to invest him at his home—Xian again sent back seals and ribbons.
translations.idiomatic: He refused repeatedly; the court ignored him and sent envoys to invest him at his door—he returned the seals.

sentences.zh: 公車不通，催使攝職。

translations.literal: The summons carriage did not connect—hastened him to assume duties.
translations.idiomatic: When memorial transport stalled, they pressed him to take up the post anyway.

sentences.zh: 咸以身無兄弟，喪祭無主，重自陳乞，乃使於官舍設靈坐。

translations.literal: Xian because he had no brothers and mourning sacrifice lacked a principal, earnestly petitioned again—thereupon had a spirit seat set in the official residence.
translations.idiomatic: With no brothers to host the offerings, he begged again—so the court let him set an ancestral seat in his office.

sentences.zh: 咸又上表曰：「臣既駑弱，不勝重任。

translations.literal: Xian again submitted a memorial: "Your servant is already dull and weak; cannot bear heavy charge.
translations.idiomatic: He laid another petition: "I am weak and unfit for heavy duty.

sentences.zh: 加在哀疚，假息日闋，陛下過意，授非所堪。

translations.literal: Added to grief in mourning, borrowed breath daily exhausted—Your Majesty over-intends, appointing what cannot be borne.
translations.idiomatic: Grief drains me day by day; Your Majesty overestimates what I can shoulder.

sentences.zh: 披露丹款，歸窮上聞，謬詔既往，終然無改。

translations.literal: Opening and laying bare loyal sincerity, returning utmost and ascending to be heard—erroneous edict already went forth—finally still no change.
translations.idiomatic: I laid my heart bare; the mistaken appointment stands unchanged.

sentences.zh: 臣雖不能滅身以全禮教，義無靦然，虛忝隆寵。

translations.literal: Though your servant cannot destroy his body to complete ritual teaching, right allows no emptiness—vainly disgracing lofty favor.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot martyr myself for ritual, yet duty forbids hollowness—I shame your kindness by holding office empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 前受嚴詔，視事之日，私心自誓，隕越為報。

translations.literal: Formerly receiving stern edict, on the day of assuming duties privately swore to dash apart in repayment.
translations.idiomatic: When I took office under your stern order I privately vowed to repay you with my life.

sentences.zh: 以貨賂流行，所宜深絕，切敕都官，以此為先。

translations.literal: Because bribery flows; what ought deeply to be cut off—urgently ordered the capital officials to take this as first.
translations.idiomatic: Bribery still runs rampant—it must be crushed; I ordered the capital bureaus to treat that as priority.

sentences.zh: 而經彌日月，未有所得。

translations.literal: Yet months pass—nothing obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Months slip by with nothing to show.

sentences.zh: 斯由陛下有以獎厲，慮於愚戇，將必死系，故自掩檢以避其鋒耳。

translations.literal: This is because Your Majesty has means to encourage—considering dull foolishness—thinking they will surely tie themselves to death; therefore self-conceal inspection to avoid its sharpness.
translations.idiomatic: People think you reward timidity—they hide evidence and dodge confrontation.

sentences.zh: 在職有日，既無赫然之舉，又不應弦垂翅，人誰復憚？

translations.literal: Holding office days—already neither blazing deeds nor responding to the bowstring drooping wings—who again fears?
translations.idiomatic: If an officer neither performs heroically nor snaps to orders, who will fear him?

sentences.zh: 故光祿大夫劉毅為司隸，聲震內外，遠近清肅。

translations.literal: Therefore Grand Counselor Liu Yi as Metropolitan Governor—reputation shook inner and outer—far and near pure and austere.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Counselor Liu Yi as Metropolitan Governor shook court and countryside—every quarter snapped upright.

sentences.zh: 非徒毅有王臣匪躬之節，亦由所奏見從，威風得伸也。

translations.literal: Not only did Yi have the integrity of a royal minister not sparing himself—also because what he memorialized was followed and awe-stretching wind obtained extension.
translations.idiomatic: Not only did Liu Yi embody selfless service—the throne acted on his impeachments, so his authority held.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「但當思必應繩中理，威風日伸，何獨劉毅！」

translations.literal: " An edict said: "Only ought to think certain responses hit the cord's middle pattern—awe-stretching wind daily extends—why only Liu Yi!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered: "Judge cases squarely and your prestige will grow—why cite only Liu Yi?"

sentences.zh: 時朝廷寬弛，豪右放恣，交私請托，朝野溷淆。

translations.literal: At the time the court was lax; powerful houses indulged freely; private connections and requests mingled—court and wilds were tangled.
translations.idiomatic: The court had gone slack; magnates ran wild with patronage until capital and countryside blurred together.

sentences.zh: 咸奏免河南尹澹、左將軍倩、廷尉高光、兼河南尹何攀等，京都肅然，貴戚懾伏。

translations.literal: Xian memorialized dismissal of Governor of Henan Dan, General of the Left Qian, Director of Trials Gao Guang, concurrent Governor of Henan He Pan, and others—the capital fell orderly and noble kin trembled.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian impeached the governors of Henan and acting Henan, the General of the Left, the chief judge—lords and kin quaked.

sentences.zh: 咸以「聖人久于其道，天下化成。

translations.literal: Xian considered "When sages long abide in their Way, All under Heaven transforms and completes.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian quoted: "When sages persist in their Way, the realm takes shape.

sentences.zh: 是以唐、虞三載考績，九年黜陟。

translations.literal: Therefore Tang and Yu examined merit every three years; in nine years dismissed and promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Tang and Yu reviewed officers triennially and promoted or demoted after nine.

sentences.zh: 其在《周禮》，三年大比。

translations.literal: As for in the Rites of Zhou, three years great comparison.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou mandated a great reckoning every third year.

sentences.zh: 孔子亦云，『三年有成』。

translations.literal: Confucius also stated, 'In three years there is accomplishment.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius too said, 'Give three years and work shows results.'

sentences.zh: 而中間以來，長吏到官，未幾便遷，百姓困于無定，吏卒疲於送迎」。

translations.literal: Yet since the middle interval, long clerks reaching office, before long then transferred—the hundred surnames are distressed by lack of stability; clerks and soldiers weary seeing off and welcoming.
translations.idiomatic: Yet lately magistrates barely unpack before transfer—the people suffer endless churn; runners collapse escorting each newcomer.

sentences.zh: 時僕射王戎兼吏部，咸奏：「戎備位臺輔，兼掌選舉，不能謐靜風俗，以凝庶績，至令人心傾動，開張浮競。

translations.literal: At that time Director Wang Rong concurrently held the Masters of Writing; Xian memorialized: "Rong occupies the terrace's chief assistance and concurrently manages selection—cannot quiet customs and stabilize manifold accomplishment—to the extent people's hearts tilt and drift and unrestrained rivalry opens wide.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong sat as Vice Director yet ran appointments—Fu Xian charged him with failing to steady morale or appointments, stirring restless ambition.

sentences.zh: 中郎李重、李義不相匡正。

translations.literal: Gentlemen-of-the-Palace Li Chong and Li Yi did not mutually correct.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Gentlemen Li Chong and Li Yi never challenged him.

sentences.zh: 請免戎等官。

translations.literal: Requested dismissal of Rong and others' offices.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian asked to dismiss Wang Rong and allies.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「政道之本，誠宜久於其職，咸奏是也。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "The foundation of government indeed ought long to abide in one's post—Xian's memorial is correct.
translations.idiomatic: The reply conceded: "Stable tenure matters—Fu Xian is right.

sentences.zh: 戎職在論道，吾所崇委，其解禁止。

translations.literal: Rong's duty lies in discussing the Way—what we greatly entrust—release prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: But Wang Rong's brief is state doctrine—we rely on him—drop the restraining order.

sentences.zh: 」御史中丞解結以咸劾戎為違典制，越局侵官，干非其分，奏免咸官。

translations.literal: " Palace Assistant Clerk Xie Jie considered Xian's impeachment of Rong violated canonical regulation—overstepped bounds intruding office—meddled beyond one's allotment—memorialized dismissal of Xian's office.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Assistant Xie Jie argued Fu Xian's impeachment broke rules and jurisdiction—he memorialized to sack Fu Xian.

sentences.zh: 詔亦不許。

translations.literal: An edict likewise did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused that too.

sentences.zh: 咸上事以為「按令，御史中丞督司百僚。

translations.literal: Xian submitted a report considering "According to ordinance, the Palace Assistant Clerk supervises and inspects the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian argued from statute: "The Palace Assistant Clerk oversees every ranked official.

sentences.zh: 皇太子以下，其在行馬內，有違法憲者皆彈糾之。

translations.literal: Below the heir apparent, those within the riding barriers who violate statutes are all impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone from the crown prince downward who breaks the law inside the cordon faces impeachment.

sentences.zh: 雖在行馬外，而監司不糾，亦得奏之。

translations.literal: Though outside the riding barriers, if supervising offices do not impeach, one may still memorialize them.
translations.idiomatic: Even beyond the cordon, if monitors fail to act, you may still memorialize the lapse.

sentences.zh: 如令之文，行馬之內有違法憲，謂禁防之事耳。

translations.literal: As the ordinance's wording runs, violation of statutes inside the riding barriers refers to matters of forbidden-zone defense.
translations.idiomatic: The statute defines "inside the barriers" as palace security breaches.

sentences.zh: 宮內禁防，外司不得而行，故專施中丞。

translations.literal: Palace interior forbidden defense—outer offices cannot carry it out—therefore it applies exclusively to the Assistant Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Outer ministries cannot police the palace—that is why the Assistant Clerk holds sole jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 今道路橋梁不修，鬥訟屠沽不絕，如此之比，中丞推責州坐，即今所謂行馬內語施於禁防。

translations.literal: Now roads and bridges go unrepaired; brawls and lawsuits among butchers and vendors never cease—cases like these the Assistant Clerk pushes blame onto the province seat—that is applying today's so-called language of "inside the barriers" to forbidden defense.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile highways crumble and street fights rage—the Assistant Clerk shifts blame to provincial seats, stretching "inside the barriers" until it covers palace guards alone.

sentences.zh: 既雲中丞督司百僚矣，何復說行馬之內乎！

translations.literal: Since it already says the Assistant Clerk supervises the hundred officials, why again speak of "inside the barriers"!
translations.idiomatic: If the edict already charges him with all officials, why harp on "inside the barriers"?

sentences.zh: 既雲百僚，而不得復說行馬之內者，內外眾官謂之百僚，則通內外矣。

translations.literal: Since it already says hundred officials, yet cannot again speak "inside the barriers"—inner and outer hosts of offices are called hundred officials—then it comprehends inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: "All officials" naturally spans palace and capital—there is no inner/outer split.

sentences.zh: 司隸所以不復說行馬內外者，禁防之事已於中丞說之故也。

translations.literal: The reason the Metropolitan Governor does not again speak riding-barrier inner and outer is because forbidden-defense matters were already stated under the Assistant Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The Metropolitan Governor omits barrier language because the Assistant Clerk already covers palace security.

sentences.zh: 中丞、司隸俱糾皇太子以下，則共對司內外矣，不為中丞專司內百僚，司隸專司外百僚。

translations.literal: Assistant Clerk and Metropolitan Governor together impeach below the heir apparent—then they jointly face inner and outer—it is not that the Assistant Clerk exclusively supervises inner hundred officials and the Metropolitan Governor exclusively supervises outer hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Both offices impeach everyone below the heir apparent—they police inner and outer together, not one for palace and one for capital.

sentences.zh: 自有中丞、司隸以來，更互奏內外眾官，惟所糾得無內外之限也。

translations.literal: Since possessing Assistant Clerk and Metropolitan Governor, they have alternately memorialized inner and outer hosts of officials—only what they impeach obtains without inner-outer limit.
translations.idiomatic: Historically both offices have rotated complaints across every ministry without territorial limits.

sentences.zh: 而結一旦橫挫臣，臣前所以不羅縷者，冀因結奏得從私願也。

translations.literal: Yet Jie suddenly humiliated your servant crosswise—your servant earlier therefore did not elaborate—hoping through Jie's memorial to obtain private wish.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xie Jie blindsided me—I stayed terse hoping his memorial would grant my leave.

sentences.zh: 今既所願不從，而敕雲但為過耳，非所不及也，以此見原。

translations.literal: Now already what was wished was not followed—yet the edict states merely fault—not what was not reached—and by this grants forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Now my request fails while the edict dismisses it as a minor slip—pardoning what never needed forgiving.

sentences.zh: 臣忝司直之任，宜當正己率人，若其有過，不敢受原，是以申陳其愚。

translations.literal: Your servant disgraces the duty of rectifying straightness—ought to rectify self and lead others—if there is fault, dares not accept forgiveness—therefore extends stating foolishness.
translations.idiomatic: I hold an office meant to model integrity; if I erred I should not hide behind pardon—so I spell out my reasoning.

sentences.zh: 司隸與中丞俱共糾皇太子以下，則從皇太子以下無所不糾也。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Governor and Assistant Clerk together impeach below the heir apparent—then from heir apparent downward nothing is not impeachable.
translations.idiomatic: Both offices may impeach anyone below the heir apparent—nothing is off limits.

sentences.zh: 得糾皇太子而不得糾尚書，臣之暗塞既所未譬。

translations.literal: Able to impeach heir apparent yet unable to impeach Ministers of the Masters of Writing—your servant's dull blockage already cannot compare.
translations.idiomatic: You may strike at the heir yet spare the Ministers of the Masters of Writing—I fail to see how that squares.

sentences.zh: 皇太子為在行馬之內邪，皇太子在行馬之內而得糾之，尚書在行馬之內而不得糾，無有此理。

translations.literal: Is the heir apparent considered inside the riding barriers or not—if the heir apparent is inside the barriers and may be impeached, Ministers of the Masters of Writing are inside the barriers yet may not be impeached—there is no such principle.
translations.idiomatic: If the palace heir sits inside the cordon and still falls under impeachment, then Ministers inside the cordon cannot be immune—logic forbids it.

sentences.zh: 此理灼然，而結以此挫臣。

translations.literal: This principle burns bright—yet Jie by this humiliates your servant.
translations.idiomatic: The logic is obvious—yet Xie Jie twists it to shame me.

sentences.zh: 臣可無恨耳，其於觀聽，無乃有怪邪！

translations.literal: Your servant may lack resentment—yet for observers and listeners—is there not strangeness!
translations.idiomatic: I can swallow pride—but what must onlookers think?

sentences.zh: 臣識石公前在殿上脫衣，為司隸荀愷所奏，先帝不以為非，于時莫謂侵官；

translations.literal: Your servant knows Lord Shi formerly on the hall stripped clothing—Metropolitan Governor Xun Kai memorialized him—the late emperor did not deem it wrong—at the time none called it encroaching office;
translations.idiomatic: Lord Shi once stripped on the palace steps—Metropolitan Governor Xun Kai impeached him—Emperor Wu saw no fault—no one cried jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 今臣裁糾尚書，而當有罪乎？

translations.literal: Now your servant barely impeaches Ministers of the Masters of Writing—yet ought to be guilty?
translations.idiomatic: Now I merely cite Ministers of the Masters of Writing—does that suddenly become a crime?

sentences.zh: 」咸累自上稱引故事，條理灼然，朝廷無以易之。

translations.literal: " Xian repeatedly personally cited precedent—the principles burned bright—the court had nothing with which to change it.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian piled precedent after precedent until the court could not refute him.

sentences.zh: 吳郡顧榮常與親故書曰：「傅長虞為司隸，勁直忠果，劾按驚人。

translations.literal: Gu Rong of Wu commandery often wrote to kin and old friends: "Fu Changyu as Metropolitan Governor—stern and straight, loyal and decisive—impeachment shocks others.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rong of Wu wrote friends that Fu Xian as Metropolitan Governor combined spine and loyalty—his indictments stunned the capital.

sentences.zh: 雖非周才，偏亮可貴也。

translations.literal: Though not all-around talent, biased brightness is valuable.
translations.idiomatic: He was no universal genius, yet his fierce integrity was priceless.

sentences.zh: 」卒官，時年五十六，詔贈司隸校尉，朝服一具、衣一襲、錢二十萬，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: " He died in office, aged fifty-six—an edict posthumously awarded Metropolitan Governor, one full court robe and cap set, one suit of clothes, two hundred thousand cash—posthumous title Zhen ("Steadfast").
translations.idiomatic: He died in harness at fifty-six; the court posthumously restored him as Metropolitan Governor, gave court robes and two hundred thousand cash, and styled him Zhen, "Steadfast."

sentences.zh: 有三子：敷、晞、纂。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Fu, Xi, Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: He left three sons—Fu, Xi, and Zuan.

sentences.zh: 長子敷嗣。

translations.literal: The eldest son Fu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest, Fu, inherited his title.

sentences.zh: 敷字穎根，清靜有道，素解屬文。

translations.literal: Fu, courtesy name Yingen, was quiet and pure with the Way; from youth understood composing texts.
translations.idiomatic: Fu bore the courtesy name Yingen—quiet, principled, and literary from youth.

sentences.zh: 除太子舍人，轉尚書郎、太傅參軍，皆不起。

translations.literal: Appointed Palace Clerk to the heir apparent; transferred Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and adjutant to the Grand Tutor—each time did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Court posts came—Palace Clerk, Masters of Writing Gentleman, Grand Tutor staff—but he refused every summons.

sentences.zh: 永嘉之亂，避地會稽，元帝引為鎮東從事中郎。

translations.literal: During the Yongjia turmoil he fled to Kuaiji—Emperor Yuan appointed him Army Adjutant on the east.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongjia chaos erupted he fled south to Kuaiji; Emperor Yuan named him adjutant to the east-army command.

sentences.zh: 素有贏疾，頻見敦喻，辭不獲免，輿病到職。

translations.literal: Long sickly and wasted; repeatedly saw earnest instruction—declined but could not escape—was carried ill to assume post.
translations.idiomatic: Chronic illness wasted him; despite imperial coaxing he could not decline—carried on a litter to his desk.

sentences.zh: 數月卒，時年四十六。

translations.literal: Several months later died, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died months later at forty-six.

sentences.zh: 晞亦有才思，為上虞令，甚有政績，卒于司徒西曹屬。

translations.literal: Xi also had literary talent—served as magistrate of Shangyu with excellent administrative record—died as Senior Clerk on the west staff of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Xi too wrote well; as magistrate of Shangyu he governed brilliantly, then died on the Minister of Education's western staff.

sentences.zh: 傅祗

translations.literal: Fu Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 祗字子莊。

translations.literal: Zhi, courtesy name Zizhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi, courtesy name Zizhuang.

sentences.zh: 父嘏，魏太常。

translations.literal: Father Gu, Wei Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fu Gu served Wei as Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 祗性至孝，早知名，以才識明練稱。

translations.literal: Zhi's nature utmost filial; early gained fame; praised for talent, judgment, clarity, and experience.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial and famed young, he won praise for seasoned judgment.

sentences.zh: 武帝始建東宮，起家太子舍人，累遷散騎黃門郎，賜爵關內侯，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu first established the Eastern Palace, from initial appointment as Palace Clerk to the heir apparent; promoted step by step to Palace Gentleman Attendant-in-Ordinary and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate; enfeoffed Secondary Marquis within the Passes—three hundred households food estate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu founded the heir's palace, Fu Zhi rose from Palace Clerk through Gentleman Attendant and Yellow Gate Gentleman, gaining a passes marquisate with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職。

translations.literal: Mother mourning removed office.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning for his mother forced him out.

sentences.zh: 及葬母，詔給太常五等吉凶導從。

translations.literal: When burying mother, edict supplied Grand Master of Ceremonies five-rank auspicious and inauspicious escort.
translations.idiomatic: For her burial the court granted Grand Master escorts for both solemn and festive ranks.

sentences.zh: 其後諸卿夫人葬給導從，自此始也。

translations.literal: Thereafter various ministers' wives' burials supplied escort—from this began.
translations.idiomatic: After that ministers' wives received the same escorts—a precedent Fu Zhi began.

sentences.zh: 服終，為滎陽太守。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, became Governor of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Once mourning ended he became Governor of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 自魏黃初大水之後，河濟泛溢，鄧艾嘗著《濟河論》，開石門而通之，至是復浸壞。

translations.literal: Since Wei Huangchu great flood afterward, Yellow River and Ji torrent overflowed—Deng Ai once composed Discourse on the Ji River—opened Stone Gate and linked them—to here again submerged and ruined.
