translations.idiomatic: After Wei Huangchu floods the Yellow River and Ji spilled everywhere; Deng Ai had penned his Ji River treatise and opened Stone Gate—yet the works again broke.

sentences.zh: 祗乃造沈萊堰，至今兗、豫無水患，百姓為立碑頌焉。

translations.literal: Zhi then built the Shenlai weir—down to today Yan and Yu have no water disaster—the hundred surnames erected a stele praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi built the Shenlai weir; Yan and Yu have stayed dry since, and locals raised a monument.

sentences.zh: 尋表兼廷尉，遷常侍、左軍將軍。

translations.literal: Shortly memorialized concurrently Director of Trials; promoted Palace Attendant and General of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he added Director of Trials, then Palace Attendant and General of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，梓宮在殯，而太傅楊駿輔政，欲悅眾心，議普進封爵。

translations.literal: When the emperor died and the coffined catafalque lay in mourning—yet Grand Tutor Yang Jun directed government—wishing to please the multitude's hearts—debated broadly advancing noble ranks.
translations.idiomatic: While the late emperor lay in state, Grand Tutor Yang Jun ruled and pushed blanket promotions to buy loyalty.

sentences.zh: 祗與駿書曰：「未有帝王始崩，臣下論功者也。

translations.literal: Zhi wrote Jun a letter: "Never has an emperor just died with subordinates debating merit.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi wrote Yang Jun: "No precedent rewards ministers while the emperor still lies unburied.

sentences.zh: 」駿不從。

translations.literal: " Jun did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun ignored him.

sentences.zh: 入為侍中。

translations.literal: Entered as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 時將誅駿，而駿不之知。

translations.literal: At the time about to execute Jun—yet Jun did not know it.
translations.idiomatic: The coup against Yang Jun was imminent—yet Yang Jun knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 祗侍駿坐，而雲龍門閉，內外不通。

translations.literal: Zhi attended Jun's sitting—yet Cloud Dragon Gate closed—inner and outer not connected.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi sat with Yang Jun when the Cloud Dragon Gate slammed—sealing court from city.

sentences.zh: 祗請與尚書武茂聽國家消息，揖而下階。

translations.literal: Zhi requested together with Minister of the Masters of Writing Wu Mao to hear national news—bowed and descended steps.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi asked Minister Wu Mao to learn what was happening outside and headed down the stairs.

sentences.zh: 茂猶坐，祗顧曰：「君非天子臣邪！

translations.literal: Mao still sat—Zhi looked back saying: "Are you not the Son of Heaven's minister!
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mao stayed put—Fu Zhi snapped, "Are you still an emperor's minister?

sentences.zh: 今內外隔絕，不知國家所在，何得安坐！

translations.literal: Now inner and outer cut off—not knowing where the state lies—how can you sit safely!
translations.idiomatic: Palace and capital are cut off—how can you lounge here?

sentences.zh: 」茂乃驚起。

translations.literal: " Mao then startled rose.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mao shot to his feet.

sentences.zh: 駿既伏誅，裴楷息瓚，駿之婿也，為亂兵所害。

translations.literal: After Jun was executed—Pei Kai's son Zan—Jun's son-in-law—was killed by mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jun fell, Pei Kai's son Pei Zan—his son-in-law—died in the mêlée.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射荀愷與楷不平，因奏楷是駿親，收付廷尉。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xun Kai bore grudge against Kai—therefore memorialized Kai was Jun's kin—arrested and delivered to Director of Trials.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Xun Kai, feuding with Pei Kai, impeached him as Yang Jun's kinsman and jailed him.

sentences.zh: 祗證楷無罪，有詔赦之。

translations.literal: Zhi testified Kai without crime—an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi vouched for Pei Kai's innocence; an edict freed him.

sentences.zh: 時又收駿官屬，祗復啟曰：「昔魯芝為曹爽司馬，斬關出赴爽，宣帝義之，尚遷青州刺史。

translations.literal: At the time also arrested Jun's subordinates—Zhi again presented: "Formerly Lu Zhi was Cao Shuang's Chief Clerk—broke gate rushing out to join Shuang—Emperor Xuan deemed it righteous—still promoted Governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jun's aides were rounded up Fu Zhi cited Lu Zhi—who broke locks to follow Cao Shuang—and Emperor Xuan still praised him.

sentences.zh: 駿之僚佐不可加罰。

translations.literal: Jun's staff assistants ought not add punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun's clerks should not be punished for loyalty.

sentences.zh: 」詔又赦之。

translations.literal: " An edict again pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict amnestied them.

sentences.zh: 祗多所維正皆如此。

translations.literal: Zhi's many corrections upheld rectitude all like this.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi intervened this way again and again.

sentences.zh: 除河南尹，未拜，遷司隸校尉。

translations.literal: Appointed Governor of Henan—before investiture—promoted Metropolitan Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Named Governor of Henan, he was elevated to Metropolitan Governor before taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 以討楊駿勳，當封郡公八千戶，固讓，減半，降封靈川縣公，千八百戶，餘二千二百戶封少子暢為武鄉亭侯。

translations.literal: For merit punishing Yang Jun—ought enfeoff commandery duke eight thousand households—firmly declined—halved—demoted enfeoff Duke of Lingchuan County—one thousand eight hundred households—remaining two thousand two hundred households enfeoff younger son Chang as Village Marquis of Wuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: His role against Yang Jun earned an eight-thousand-household commandery dukedom—he refused until it shrank to Lingchuan County duke at eighteen hundred households, diverting twenty-two hundred to his son Chang as Wuxiang village marquis.

sentences.zh: 又以本封賜兄子雋為東明亭侯。

translations.literal: Again with original enfeoff gifted elder brother's son Jun as Village Marquis of Dongming.
translations.idiomatic: He also passed his original stipend to nephew Jun as Dongming village marquis.

sentences.zh: 楚王瑋之矯詔也，祗以聞奏稽留，免官。

translations.literal: When Prince Chu Wei forged the edict—Zhi because news memorial delayed—removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Sima Wei forged orders Fu Zhi delayed reporting—costing his post.

sentences.zh: 期年，遷光祿勳，復以公事免。

translations.literal: One full year—promoted Minister of the Household—again removed on public business.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he rose to Minister of the Household, then lost office again over policy.

sentences.zh: 氐人齊萬年舉兵反，以祗為行安西軍司，加常侍，率安西將軍夏侯駿討平之。

translations.literal: Di tribesman Qi Wannian raised troops in rebellion—appointed Zhi acting Western Pacification Army supervisor—added Palace Attendant—led General of the West Xiahou Jun to pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Wannian rebelled Fu Zhi served as acting army supervisor for the west, with Palace Attendant rank, under General Xiahou Jun.

sentences.zh: 遷衛尉，以風疾遜位，就拜常侍，食卿祿秩，賜錢及床帳等。

translations.literal: Promoted Commandant of the Guards—because wind illness yielded position—received appointment Palace Attendant—ate ministerial salary rank—gifted cash and bedding etc.
translations.idiomatic: He became Commandant of the Guards, stepped down for palsy, kept Palace Attendant stipends, and received cash and bedding.

sentences.zh: 尋加光祿大夫，門施行馬。

translations.literal: Shortly added Grand Counselor—gate applied riding barriers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he added Grand Counselor and gate barriers like a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 及趙王倫輔政，以為中書監，常侍如故，以鎮眾心。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhao Lun directed government—appointed him Director of the Palace Secretariat—Palace Attendant as before—to steady popular hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhao Lun made him Palace Secretariat Director to steady nerves.

sentences.zh: 祗辭之以疾，倫遣御史輿祗就職。

translations.literal: Zhi declined citing illness—Lun dispatched censors to carry Zhi to assume duties.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness—Sima Lun sent censors to haul him to his desk.

sentences.zh: 王戎、陳准等相與言曰：「傅公在事，吾屬無憂矣。

translations.literal: Wang Rong, Chen Zhun and others mutually said: "With Duke Fu in office—we have no worries.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong and Chen Zhun said, "With Fu Zhi on duty we sleep soundly.

sentences.zh: 」其為物所倚信如此。

translations.literal: " He was thus relied on and trusted by things.
translations.idiomatic: The realm leaned on him that heavily.

sentences.zh: 倫篡，又為右光祿、開府，加侍中。

translations.literal: Lun usurped—again became Right Grand Counselor, establishing headquarters—added Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Lun seized the throne Fu Zhi became Right Grand Counselor with independent headquarters.

sentences.zh: 惠帝還宮，祗以經受偽職請退，不許。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui returned to palace—Zhi because passing through false office requested retirement—not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui's return left Fu Zhi asking to resign for serving the usurper—the court refused.

sentences.zh: 初，倫之篡也，孫秀與義陽王威等十餘人預撰儀式禪文。

translations.literal: Earlier when Lun usurped—Sun Xiu with Prince Yiyang Wei and more than ten others pre-drafted ritual abdication text.
translations.idiomatic: During Sima Lun's coup Sun Xiu and Prince Sima Wei pre-wrote the abdication liturgy.

sentences.zh: 及倫敗，齊王冏收侍中劉逵、常侍騶捷、杜育、黃門郎陸機、右丞周導、王尊等付廷尉。

translations.literal: When Lun failed—Prince Qi Min arrested Palace Attendant Liu Kui, Palace Attendants Zou Jie, Du Yu, Yellow Gate Gentleman Lu Ji, Right Assistant Director Zhou Dao, Wang Zun et al.—delivered to Director of Trials.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Lun fell, Prince Sima Min jailed Liu Kui, Lu Ji, and others.

sentences.zh: 以禪文出中書，復議處祗罪，會赦得原。

translations.literal: Because abdication text issued from Palace Secretariat—again debated punishing Zhi's crime—met amnesty and obtained forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Because the abdication edict came from the Secretariat they debated Fu Zhi's guilt—an amnesty spared him.

sentences.zh: 後以禪文草本非祗所撰，於是詔復光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later because abdication draft in grass was not what Zhi composed—thereupon edict restored Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Later they learned Fu Zhi never penned the draft—his Grand Counselor title returned.

sentences.zh: 子宣，尚弘農公主。

translations.literal: Son Xuan married Princess of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu Xuan married the Princess of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太子少傅，上章遜位還第。

translations.literal: Shortly promoted Junior Tutor to the heir apparent—submitted memorial declining office returning residence.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Junior Tutor—he begged to retire home.

sentences.zh: 及成都王穎為太傅，復以祗為少傅，加侍中。

translations.literal: When Prince Chengdu Ying became Grand Tutor—again appointed Zhi Junior Tutor—added Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chengdu Ying became Grand Tutor he recalled Fu Zhi as Junior Tutor with Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 懷帝即位，遷光祿大夫、侍中，未拜，加右僕射、中書監。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended—promoted Grand Counselor and Palace Attendant—before investiture—added Right Vice Director and Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai promoted him toward Grand Counselor and Secretariat Director before the seals arrived.

sentences.zh: 時太傅東海王越輔政，祗既居端右，每宣君臣謙光之道，由此上下雍穆。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Tutor Prince Donghai Yue directed government—Zhi already occupied the chief right—every time proclaimed ruler-minister yielding glory—thereby high and low harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: While Prince Donghai Yue ruled, Fu Zhi held the chief seat and preached humility between sovereign and ministers.

sentences.zh: 祗明達國體，朝廷制度多所經綜。

translations.literal: Zhi understood national bodies—court regulations many managed through him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi mastered state ritual and shaped institutions.

sentences.zh: 曆左光祿、開府，行太子太傅，侍中如故。

translations.literal: Passed through Left Grand Counselor, establishing headquarters—acting Grand Tutor to the heir apparent—Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He rotated through Left Grand Counselor with headquarters, acting heir's tutor, keeping Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 疾篤遜位，不許。

translations.literal: Critically ill yielded position—not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Deathly ill he offered to resign—the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒，以足疾，詔版輿上殿，不拜。

translations.literal: Promoted Minister of Education—because foot illness—edict palanquin ascend hall—no bow.
translations.idiomatic: Made Minister of Education on a litter—excused from bows.

sentences.zh: 大將軍苟晞表請遷都，使祗出詣河陰，修理舟楫，為水行之備。

translations.literal: General-in-Chief Gou Xi memorialized requesting moving capital—ordered Zhi go out to Heyin—repair boats—prepare water travel.
translations.idiomatic: General Gou Xi urged relocating the court and sent Fu Zhi to Heyin to ready boats.

sentences.zh: 及洛陽陷沒，遂共建行台，推祗為盟主，以司徒、持節、大都督諸軍事傳檄四方。

translations.literal: When Luoyang fell—thereupon together erected traveling headquarters—pushed Zhi as covenant chief—with Minister of Education, credential-bearing Commander-in-Chief All Military Affairs—issued manifestos to four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: After Luoyang fell allies built a mobile command and named Fu Zhi covenant leader as Minister of Education and supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 遣子宣將公主與尚書令和郁赴告方伯征義兵，祗自屯盟津小城，宣弟暢行河陰令，以待宣。

translations.literal: Dispatched son Xuan leading princess together with Minister of the Masters of Writing He Yu to hurry inform regional shepherds seeking righteous troops—Zhi personally camped small town at Meng ford—Xuan's younger brother Chang acted Heyin magistrate—awaiting Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Fu Xuan and He Yu to rally governors while he held Meng ford; younger son Chang governed Heyin pending reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 祗以暴疾薨，時年六十九。

translations.literal: Zhi died suddenly of illness—aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi died suddenly at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 祗自以義誠不終，力疾手筆敕厲其二子宣、暢，辭旨深切，覽者莫不感激慷慨。

translations.literal: Zhi himself because righteous sincerity did not reach completion—forced illness hand wrote edict urging his two sons Xuan and Chang—word intent deep-cutting—readers none not moved inspired generous.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling his loyal mission unfinished he scribbled dying orders to Fu Xuan and Fu Chang—every reader wept.

sentences.zh: 祗著文章駁論十餘萬言。

translations.literal: Zhi composed essays refuting debates over one hundred thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: He left more than a hundred thousand characters of essays and rebuttals.

sentences.zh: 宣字世弘。

translations.literal: Xuan courtesy name Shihong.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan bore the courtesy name Shihong.

sentences.zh: 年六歲喪繼母，哭泣如成人，中表異之。

translations.literal: Age six lost stepmother—weeping like adult—cousins marveled.
translations.idiomatic: At six he mourned his stepmother like a grown man—kin marveled.

sentences.zh: 及長，好學，趙王倫以為相國掾、尚書郎、太子中舍人，遷司徒西曹掾。

translations.literal: When grown loved learning—Prince Zhao Lun appointed him Chancellor of State clerk, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, Palace Clerk to the heir apparent—promoted Senior Clerk on the west staff of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Adult, studious, Sima Lun named him to staff posts until Senior Clerk on the Minister of Education's western bureau.

sentences.zh: 去職，累遷為秘書丞、驃騎從事中郎。

translations.literal: Left office—promoted step by step Secretary Manager, Army Adjutant to the Cavalry-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving office he rose to secretary director and adjutant to the chief cavalry command.

sentences.zh: 惠帝至自長安，以宣為左丞，不就，遷黃門郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui arrived from Chang'an—appointed Xuan Left Assistant Director—did not take office—promoted Yellow Gate Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui returned from Chang'an he offered Fu Xuan Left Assistant Director—Fu Xuan declined—then named Yellow Gate Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 懷帝即位，轉吏部郎，又為御史中丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended the throne, [Fu Xuan] was transferred Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and again served as Palace Assistant Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Huai he rotated through the Masters of Writing and again became Palace Assistant Clerk.

sentences.zh: 卒年四十九，無子，以暢子沖為嗣。

translations.literal: He died aged forty-nine; having no son, Chang's son Chong was appointed heir.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-nine without sons; his nephew Fu Chong, Fu Chang's boy, inherited his line.

sentences.zh: 暢字世道。

translations.literal: Chang, courtesy name Shidao.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chang bore the courtesy name Shidao.

sentences.zh: 年五歲，父友見而戲之，解暢衣，取其金環與侍者，暢不之惜，以此賞之。

translations.literal: Age five—a friend of his father saw him and teased him—removed Chang's clothing—took his gold ring for an attendant—Chang did not grudge it—for this [the friend] praised him.
translations.idiomatic: At five a friend of his father teased him: stripping his jacket and pocketing his gold ring for a servant—Fu Chang shrugged it off, and the man praised his aplomb.

sentences.zh: 年未弱冠，甚有重名。

translations.literal: Age not yet capped—had very heavy reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Before his capping ceremony he was already celebrated.

sentences.zh: 以選入侍講東宮，為秘書丞。

translations.literal: Selected to attend lectures in the Eastern Palace—became Secretary Manager.
translations.idiomatic: Chosen as lecturer in the heir's palace, he rose to Secretary Manager.

sentences.zh: 尋沒于石勒，勒以為大將軍右司馬。

translations.literal: Shortly fell captive to Shi Le—Le appointed him Senior Clerk on the right of the Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Captured soon afterward by Shi Le, he was named senior clerk on Shi Le's staff.

sentences.zh: 諳識朝儀，恆居機密，勒甚重之。

translations.literal: Thoroughly knew court ceremony—always dwelt in confidential matters—Le heavily esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered court ritual and Shi Le's inner councils; the warlord prized him.

sentences.zh: 作《晉諸公敘贊》二十二卷，又為《公卿故事》九卷。

translations.literal: Composed Narrative Encomia of Jin Nobles twenty-two fascicles—again composed Ducal Ministers' Precedents nine fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote twenty-two fascicles of Narrative Encomia for Jin grandees and nine fascicles of Ducal Ministers' Precedents.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: Died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子詠，過江為交州刺史、太子右率。

translations.literal: Son Yong—crossed the Yangzi—became Inspector of Jiaozhou—General of the Right Guard to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu Yong crossed south to serve as Inspector of Jiaozhou and Right Guard to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 【史評】

translations.literal: 【Historians' Commentary】
translations.idiomatic: Historians' Commentary

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：武帝覽觀四方，平章百姓，永言啟沃，任切爭臣。

translations.literal: The historians state: Emperor Wu surveyed the four quarters, harmonized the hundred surnames—ever speaking of enlightening nurture—duty pressing upon remonstrating ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: Emperor Wu scanned the realm and steadied the common people; he hungered for honest counsel and leaned hard on his remonstrators.

sentences.zh: 傅玄體強直之姿，懷匪躬之操，抗辭正色，補闕弼違，諤諤當朝，不忝其職者矣。

translations.literal: Fu Xuan embodied the posture of stern uprightness; he cherished the integrity of selfless sacrifice; he confronted wrong with blunt speech and stern countenance; he repaired omissions and corrected deviations; he spoke fearlessly in court—truly he did not disgrace his office.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan carried himself with iron integrity, risking everything to speak plain truth and plug policy gaps—he was every inch the remonstrator his post demanded.

sentences.zh: 及乎位居三獨，彈擊是司，遂能使台閣生風，貴戚斂手。

translations.literal: When he rose among the Three Independents and impeachment was his charge, he could make the ministries feel a chill wind and force even imperial in-laws to fold their hands.
translations.idiomatic: Once he joined the Three Independents and turned impeachment into his métier, the ministries trembled and great clans flinched.

sentences.zh: 雖前代鮑、葛，何以加之！

translations.literal: Though the Bao and Ge of former ages—how could one add to that!
translations.idiomatic: Not even Han's famed scourges Bao Xuan and Ge Gong outdid him.

sentences.zh: 然而惟此褊心，乏弘雅之度，驟聞競爽，為物議所譏，惜哉！

translations.literal: Yet only this narrow heart—lacking breadth and grace—at sudden news of competing excellence—was mocked by public opinion—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Yet his temper ran narrow and lacked magnanimity; his readiness to clash drew ridicule—what a pity!

sentences.zh: 古人取戒于韋弦，良有以也。

translations.literal: The ancients took warning from hard bow and loose string—indeed there was cause.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients prized both taut bow and yielding strap as reminders—his story proves why.

sentences.zh: 長虞風格凝峻，弗墜家聲。

translations.literal: Changyu's manner was austere and towering—he did not let the family's renown slip.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian's stern dignity upheld the Fu name.

sentences.zh: 及其納諫汝南，獻書臨晉，居諒直之地，有先見之明矣。

translations.literal: Reaching his accepting remonstrance from Runan and presenting memorials at Linjin—dwelling in straightforward station—he showed prescience.
translations.idiomatic: When he pressed Prince Runan with counsel and laid strategy at Linjin, his blunt station proved prophetic.

sentences.zh: 傅祗名父之子，早樹風猷，崎嶇危亂之朝，匡救君臣之際，卒能保全祿位，可謂有道存焉。

translations.literal: Fu Zhi was the son of a famed father; early he set up manner and planning; in a perilous, chaotic court he rescued ruler and minister at their crises—finally able to preserve salary and station—one may say the Way dwelt in him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi, heir to a celebrated father, charted his own course through chaos, steadying sovereign and ministers alike and keeping honor and office—a man in whom the Way clearly rested.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：鶉觚貞諒，實惟朝望。

translations.literal: Encomium says: Chungu's steadfast sincerity—truly was the court's expectation.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: Baron of Chungu—steadfast faith—the court's very polestar.

sentences.zh: 志厲強直，性乖夷曠。

translations.literal: Aspiration fierce and strong straight—nature contrary to easy breadth.
translations.idiomatic: His will drove fierce integrity; his temperament spurned fashionable looseness.

sentences.zh: 長虞剛簡，無虧風尚。

translations.literal: Changyu stern and plain—without losing moral bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian's austerity never tarnished the family's moral stature.

sentences.zh: 子莊才識，爰膺袞職。

translations.literal: Zizhuang's talent and judgment—thereupon assumed ceremonial robe duties.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zizhuang's gifts earned him the highest ministerial robes.

sentences.zh: 忠績未申，泉途遽逼。

translations.literal: Loyal deeds not yet extended—spring road hastily pressed.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal service cut short—death hurried him down the dark road.
